name: Khalifa Port Container Terminal 2 (CSP Abu Dhabi)
value: 35-year concession (plus a 5-year option) signed in 2016; about $738m present value, including about $322m of capital spending; opened 2018
lender_builder: COSCO Shipping Ports (90% of voting rights); AD Ports 10%
china_gets: Control of a Gulf container hub next to the KEZAD free zone
host_position: AD Ports promotes the terminal as a Belt and Road hub
confidence_reason: Terms are in COSCO's stock-exchange filing and on AD Ports' own pages

name: Suspected Chinese military construction at Khalifa Port
value: No figures; US intelligence reported construction in 2021 that the UAE halted under US pressure, and leaked documents said work resumed in 2023
china_gets: A possible military logistics foothold in the Gulf
host_position: The UAE says the facilities were never military; US officials said there was no sign of an operational base
confidence_reason: Based on leaked US intelligence and anonymous officials (WSJ, Washington Post); denied by the UAE

name: Haifa Bayport
value: About a 25-year operating concession (won in 2015, opened September 2021); the port cost 5.5bn shekels (about $1.7bn), built by Israel
china_gets: Operation of a new Mediterranean container terminal next to the Haifa naval base
host_position: Israel sought competition in the port sector; US officials raised security concerns
confidence_reason: Concession and timeline confirmed by SIPG Bayport, Israel Ports Company and Reuters

name: Tel Aviv Red Line light rail (tunnelling)
value: Underground sections won by consortia with Chinese firms (about $800m eastern segment award, 2015); CCECC holds 19% of the operator Tevel
lender_builder: China Railway Tunnel Group; China Civil Engineering Construction Corp (CCECC)
china_gets: Construction contracts and a minority share of the line's operating company
host_position: Israel ran open tenders; INSS has raised concerns about the Chinese involvement
confidence_reason: Contract value from ENR; operator share reported by INSS

name: China-Egypt TEDA Suez Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone
value: 7.34 sq km developed since 2008, plus 2.86 sq km added in 2025 ($100m of infrastructure); about 200 companies and $3bn invested
china_gets: A manufacturing base at the southern entrance of the Suez Canal, with tariff-free access to Egypt's trade partners
host_position: Egypt calls it a priority and offered TEDA more land
confidence_reason: Egyptian state media and HKTDC research

name: New Administrative Capital business district (Iconic Tower)
value: $3.5bn contract with CSCEC; about 85% financed by Chinese bank loans ($843m, $1.36bn and $800m; 13.5-year term) with an Egyptian sovereign guarantee
lender_builder: ICBC-led syndicates incl. China Exim and Bank of China; CSCEC built it and now operates it
china_gets: Construction and operating contracts, plus a guaranteed loan
host_position: Egypt calls the new capital the engine of future growth
confidence_reason: Loan details in AidData records and the ICBC case study

name: Cairo-10th of Ramadan light rail (LRT)
value: $1.24bn contract; China Exim loan of about $1.2bn (January 2019); 66km line that opened in July 2022
lender_builder: China Exim; AVIC International and China Railway Group; CRRC trains
china_gets: Construction contract, train sales and loan repayment
host_position: Egypt says the line connects Cairo to the new capital
confidence_reason: Loan and contract confirmed by Reuters, Railway Journal and AidData

name: Kumport container terminal (Ambarli, Istanbul)
lender_builder: COSCO Pacific 40%, China Merchants 40%, CIC Capital 20% of the consortium
china_gets: Control of Turkey's third-largest container terminal on the Bosporus route
host_position: Turkey called it the largest Chinese direct investment in the country
confidence_reason: Deal confirmed in COSCO's filing and Turkey's investment office

name: Emba Hunutlu coal power plant
value: 1,320 MW; about $1.7bn; $1.381bn syndicated buyer's credit from CDB, ICBC and Bank of China
lender_builder: SPIC / Shanghai Electric Power; Chinese bank syndicate
china_gets: Ownership of a large coal plant and loan income
host_position: Turkey wanted more electricity supply; environmental groups opposed it
confidence_reason: Loan in AidData; project details from industry sources

name: Sino-Oman Industrial City, Duqm
value: 1,172 hectares under a usufruct agreement signed in 2016; $10.7bn pledged but only a few projects built
china_gets: A foothold in a special economic zone on the Arabian Sea
host_position: Oman markets Duqm as a logistics hub; progress has been slow
confidence_reason: Land deal confirmed by Oman's Duqm zone authority (SEZAD); the investment figure is a pledge, not money spent

name: YASREF refinery, Yanbu
value: 400,000 barrels/day refinery; Sinopec holds 37.5%; opened by Xi Jinping and King Salman in 2016
china_gets: Part-ownership of a large Red Sea refinery
host_position: Saudi Arabia is expanding it into petrochemicals with Sinopec (2025 framework)
confidence_reason: Ownership and output figures from Aramco and YASREF

name: Aramco refinery joint ventures in China (Panjin HAPCO, Rongsheng, Fujian)
value: 30% of the 300,000 b/d HAPCO plant; 10% of Rongsheng with 480,000 b/d crude supply; new 320,000 b/d Fujian JV with Sinopec; marker at Aramco's head office, but the plants are in China
lender_builder: Saudi Aramco with NORINCO, Rongsheng and Sinopec
china_gets: Long-term Saudi crude supply locked into Chinese refineries
host_position: Saudi Arabia is securing China as a crude market
confidence_reason: From Aramco press releases and Reuters

name: Qatar North Field East LNG stake and 27-year supply deal
value: 27-year deal for 4m tonnes/yr of LNG (2022), plus a second 27-year deal (2023); Sinopec holds 1.25% of North Field East
china_gets: Long-term LNG supply and a small stake in the gas project
host_position: Qatar is locking in Asian buyers
confidence_reason: Confirmed by Reuters, S&P Global and Qatar's state news agency

name: Chinese purchases of Iranian oil
value: About 1.48m barrels/day in 2024, roughly 90% or more of Iran's oil exports (Kpler)
lender_builder: Independent ('teapot') Chinese refiners; ships that hide their movements
host_position: Iran depends on China as its main oil buyer
confidence_reason: Volumes are tanker-tracking estimates (Kpler); China reports no Iranian imports in its official data

name: China-Iran 25-year cooperation agreement
value: Signed 27 March 2021; the text has not been published; a reported $400bn of Chinese investment has not happened
china_gets: An agreement on paper only: no confirmed projects, spending or terms
host_position: Iran presents it as a strategic partnership
confidence_reason: Text unpublished; the $400bn figure comes from press reports and has not been confirmed

name: Tehran-Mashhad railway electrification
value: $1.5bn China Exim loan signed in 2017 for a 926km line; China pulled out in January 2021
host_position: Iran says it is going ahead on its own
confidence_reason: Loan signing documented; China's exit reported by Iranian state-linked media

name: Iraq-China oil-for-reconstruction deal (1,000 schools)
value: At least 100,000 barrels/day of oil sales feed an account for Chinese-built projects; the first project, 1,000 schools, was built by PowerChina (679) and Sinotec (321)
host_position: Iraq says the schools project is delivering; critics worry about the long-term terms
confidence_reason: Framework confirmed by Iraq's state news agency (INA) and AidData; the full terms have not been published

name: CNPC stakes in Rumaila, Halfaya and West Qurna 1
value: 46.4% of Rumaila, 45% of Halfaya, 32.7% of West Qurna 1 (operator since 2024); Chinese firms produce about two-thirds of Iraq's oil
china_gets: Equity oil from Iraq's largest fields
host_position: Iraq is courting Chinese investors to raise output
confidence_reason: Stakes from Iraq's natural resources transparency committee (NRTC) and Reuters; production share from S&P

name: Attarat oil-shale power plant
value: 554 MW; about $2.1bn; $1.58bn syndicated loan from ICBC, Bank of China, CCB and China Exim
lender_builder: Chinese bank syndicate (Sinosure insured); Guangdong Energy holds part of the owner
host_position: Jordan sought arbitration over a tariff it calls unfair (about 17 US cents/kWh) and lost in 2024
confidence_reason: Loan in AidData; the arbitration outcome was reported by Jordan's state news agency and Jus Mundi
